summary: Discovery call focused on Private/VPC deployment options. Archon is leaning toward a private deployment behind their AWS VPC with strict egress controls and cross-account peering. Main risks: data residency, region constraints (APAC), KMS integration, and approval timeline for security. Agreed to follow up with detailed network runbook and technical deep dive for benchmarking.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Sasha (Archon Head Infra), Miguel (Archon DevOps), Priya (Archon Security), Omar (Archon PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Jonah and Lena from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone?
[00:15] Sasha: Hi, Sasha here. We're excited to talk through private deployment options. We're trying to understand networking patterns — peering, private endpoints, stuff like that.
[00:25] Miguel: Yep, apologies for being a bit late. We're especially concerned about egress and our SOC2 constraints.
[00:35] Maya: Totally. Today we'll cover the different private deployment flavors—VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoint, Transit Gateway patterns—and map that to your constraints like region residency and KMS integration.
[00:47] Jonah: Quick note, we often refer to the product as Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicated depending on committed capacity. In this convo I'll say Redwood Private to mean customer-managed network deployment.
[01:05] Priya: Good. The security team will need details on key management (KMS/HSM), audit logs, and where logs are stored — cloud region and retention.
[01:15] Lena: We have a standard security pack we can share — SOC2, ISO docs, and our guide for customer-managed KMS. I'll drop the links after the call.

[02:12] Miguel: Our infra is mainly in aws-eu-west-1 and aws-ap-southeast-1 for APAC. We need low-latency access from EU and APAC users. Can Redwood run Private in multiple regions?
[02:28] Jonah: Yes, we support multi-region Private deployments. Typically customers deploy one private control plane in their primary region and optionally replicate inference endpoints to other regions. For strict data residency you can keep everything in-region.
[02:44] Sasha: Are there limitations with cross-account peering? We prefer to keep Redwood in a different AWS account for billing separation.
[02:55] Maya: That's common. We support cross-account VPC peering and Transit Gateway attachments. We provide terraform templates for peering and IAM roles to allow controlled access. If you want Transit Gateway, that's supported too — depends on your topology and scale.

[04:05] Omar: For private endpoints, is it PrivateLink or something like an internal ALB?
[04:13] Jonah: We can expose private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint) or via internal NLB/ALB fronting the service in your VPC. PrivateLink reduces cross-region complexity if you need inter-account access without peering. However, PrivateLink has IP limits and may complicate large-scale traffic patterns.
[04:35] Miguel: What about egress? We need to ensure no unintended internet egress for requests or model downloads.
[04:45] Lena: Model artifacts are either pulled from a customer-managed S3 or can be downloaded during onboarding. For strict no-egress policies, we can host model weights in your S3 and we run inside your VPC so network does not need internet access. Bootstrapping the runtime may require outbound to our images registry unless you mirror images — we support air-gapped images via private registry.

[06:02] Priya: KMS — we require customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[06:12] Jonah: Yes, we support using your customer-managed KMS keys. For Private we can configure encryption materials to use your CMKs. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can discuss patterns (bring-your-own-HSM or cloud HSM). We'll need to coordinate IAM roles and key policies.
[06:28] Miguel: Ok, we need to see the IAM trust boundaries.

[07:40] Sasha: On latency: our latency SLO for critical flows is <100ms for token generation from EU region. Does Redwood support colocating inference nodes per region?
[07:52] Jonah: Yes. For sub-100ms you'd want inference nodes in eu-west-1 and possibly ap-southeast-1. Dedicated capacity/reserved pools in each region help. There's a tradeoff: more regions increases cost. We can provide guidance based on your QPS and token sizes.

[09:30] Maya: Can you share rough traffic patterns — bursts, sustained throughput, typical prompt lengths?
[09:36] Omar: We're seeing bursts up to 120 TPS for embeddings and maybe 25 rps for generation during peak. Prompts average 120 tokens, responses 80 tokens.
[09:47] Jonah: That helps. We'll run a capacity/throughput estimate and propose a config (batching, KV cache) to meet latency/cost targets.

[11:05] Miguel: IP whitelisting — we want to restrict only a short list of egress addresses. Is that possible?
[11:12] Lena: In Private, the service runs in your VPC so outbound IPs can be managed by your NAT Gateway or egress appliances. If you use PrivateLink, we can provide a set of interface endpoints and minimal reachable IPs. For hosted endpoints (Redwood-hosted), we provide fixed IP ranges to whitelist, but since you're aiming for Private, your VPC controls it.

[12:50] Priya: Audit logs — we need a tamper-evident trail of requests, who accessed what model, and redaction rules.
[12:58] Maya: Redwood provides request-level audit logs with token-level metadata. For private deployments, logs can be delivered to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) and we support retention policies. We'll also include options for immutable logs and integration with your logging pipeline.

[14:15] Sasha: Network peering templates — do you have terraform templates?
[14:20] Jonah: Yes, we have terraform and CloudFormation templates for peering, TGW attachments, and PrivateLink setup. We'll share a sample repo.

[15:50] Miguel: What about certs — mTLS between our services and Redwood endpoints?
[15:56] Lena: We can support mutual TLS. For internal endpoints we often rely on AWS-managed certs (ACM) or customer-provided certs. mTLS is an option if you need client cert enforcement.

[17:10] Omar: APAC region — our compliance folks need data to remain in APAC for certain customers. Can we have a fully isolated APAC deployment?
[17:20] Jonah: Yes, you can. We can deploy the inference nodes and model storage in ap-southeast-1 and keep logs within that region. There is some extra coordination for cross-region control plane components but we can architect it so the control plane either resides in-region or you use a regional control plane copy.

[18:45] Priya: Compliance review: will Redwood's private deployment meet our SOC2/ISO audit needs?
[18:53] Maya: Many of our financial customers run Private with SOC2/ISO and we provide the necessary artifacts and operations runbooks. We'll share our compliance pack and also a checklist you can give to your auditors.

[20:05] Sasha: One objection from procurement is timeline; enterprise security approval can take 6–8 weeks, same for networking teams. What's typical for Redwood Private onboarding?
[20:18] Jonah: For a simple pilot, ~2–4 weeks if you can provide network access and mirror images. Full production with multi-region and dedicated capacity is typically 6–10 weeks depending on approvals. We'll work with you on a phased approach: pilot (single-region), then roll out.

[22:40] Miguel: Any gotchas with Transit Gateway? We use TGW for cross-account connectivity and prefer not to create a bunch of peering relationships.
[22:50] Lena: Transit Gateway is supported and we often recommend TGW for larger setups. The main considerations are route table complexity and whether you want centralized or decentralized inspection (e.g., security appliances). We'll provide recommended route table entries.

[24:05] Omar: Licenses and pricing question — if we run dedicated capacity in two regions what does the pricing look like?
[24:12] Maya: We typically quote reserved capacity plus smaller baseline for burst. I'll send a pricing sheet after this call; for discovery we can give a ballpark. Pricing also depends on model family, quantization, and throughput requirements.

[25:40] Miguel: Are there any managed connectors for SAML/SOC tooling?
[25:45] Jonah: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and can forward audit logs to your SIEM.

[27:00] Priya: Data retention — we need to ensure we can purge logs or set retention to 90 days.
[27:08] Lena: You can control retention in your logging stack for private deployment. For any metadata Redwood stores (control plane), we can configure retention per contract; we have options for minimal retention or longer windows depending on legal.

[29:30] Sasha: Next technical deep dive — Miguel and I want to walk through our VPC diagram and run a quick peering exercise with your team. Can we do that next week?
[29:40] Maya: Absolutely. Jonah and Lena can lead that. What's your availability?
[29:46] Miguel: Early next week Tue/Wed afternoon UTC works.

[31:00] Jonah: For the deep dive we'll want your VPC CIDR ranges, current TGW attachments, any firewall appliances, and whether you require egress inspection. Also whether you prefer PrivateLink or TGW.

[32:12] Miguel: One small nit — on our side we have a hard requirement that no model weights leave AWS region. You mentioned mirroring; how does that work?
[32:22] Lena: We support your requirement. You can host model artifacts in your S3 bucket in-region. Our deployment scripts will pull artifacts from that location during provisioning; no external download required. For managed images we offer image mirrors or pre-baked AMIs you can import into your account.

[33:50] Priya: On key rotation policies — we'll need to rotate CMKs quarterly and have an approval flow.
[33:58] Jonah: That aligns with standard AWS KMS rotation. We'll document recommended rotation plans and key policy snippets to ensure Redwood services maintain access through rotation windows.

[35:20] Omar: Are there any metrics you export for health & performance?
[35:25] Maya: Yes—token latency, per-route QPS, GPU utilization, error rates. For Private we expose these to your monitoring stack and via the Redwood Console (if you opt in).

[36:45] Sasha: We might want to run a short benchmark comparing hosted vs private in our APAC region. What do you need from us?
[36:54] Jonah: We'll need sample prompts, expected concurrency, and a small dataset. We'll set up a pilot cluster in ap-southeast-1 and run controlled tests. We'll also include quantized model variant suggestions to reduce cost.

[38:10] Miguel: Network ACLs — do you require any inbound ports open beyond the PrivateLink endpoints?
[38:18] Lena: Typically only the interface endpoints and health-check ports are needed. We'll give a hardened list.

[39:50] Priya: For legal, we'll need liability / data handling terms. Is Redwood open to standard finance-redline negotiations?
[39:58] Maya: Yes, enterprise legal is used to finance redlines. We'll involve our legal team once you indicate you want to proceed; approval timelines vary but we can provide standard contract templates.

[41:05] Sasha: Any known production issues customers hit during cross-region deployments?
[41:12] Jonah: Mostly by misconfigured route tables or missing NAT for OS-level updates. We provide a checklist and pre-check scripts to validate network config before onboarding which catches most issues.

[42:30] Omar: Great. Can we recap next steps?
[42:36] Maya: Sure. Recap: 1) We'll send the security/compliance pack and private deployment runbook (Lena). 2) Jonah will schedule the technical deep dive for Tue/Wed next week and bring a peering template. 3) Maya will send pricing ballpark and trial details. 4) Archon to share VPC diagram and egress rules.

[43:05] Miguel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[43:10] Priya: Thanks.
[43:15] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links (SOC2 doc link: https://redwood.example.com/compliance and sample terraform repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-templates).
[43:30] Sasha: Appreciate it. Bye.
[43:35] Maya: Bye everyone.
